name: Polar sea ice
summary: Arctic sea ice 1.51M km² and Antarctic 1.45M km² below average on 11 Nov; neither at a record low
state: On 11 Nov Arctic sea-ice extent was 8.84 million km², about 1.51 million below the 1981–2010 average and fourth-lowest for the date, as autumn refreeze continued. Antarctic extent was 15.09 million km², about 1.45 million below average and third-lowest for the date (NSIDC). Both are past the −1.0 million Watch line, and neither pole is at a record low for the date.
for_you: Low sea ice mainly affects Arctic and Antarctic ecosystems and communities, and over time adds to ocean warming. There is no direct, immediate effect on daily life in the UK.
rubric_hit: Watch: both poles below −1.0M km² (Arctic −1.51, Antarctic −1.45); no record low for the date

sources.title: NSIDC — Sea Ice Index (Arctic Sea Ice News tools)

why: Sea ice reflects sunlight and regulates ocean circulation; record lows accelerate warming.
drivers: Air and ocean temperatures, winds, season.

rubric.alert: Either pole at a record low for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Arctic and Antarctic extent anomalies both above −1.0 million km² vs 1981–2010.
